Problem Summary:

See https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/35904.

### What is changed and how it works?

When `increment-import` is enabled, this PR will allocate autoid globally before restoring starts.  Thus we can import data to a partition that won't conflict with normal read/write operations to other partitions.

issue_context.title: lightning: allocate autoid globally across all tidb instances
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

We are discussing the local backend below.

In https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/35148, we supported disabling pd scheduler by key range, so that we can import data to a table without significant impact on other tables which are used by online services. 

Further, we want to support partition-level online import. That is to say, lightning can import data to a specific partition. Meanwhile, any read/write operations to other partitions on the same table are allowed and safe. There is no data loss or data corruption. To achieve this goal, we must avoid any autoid conflicts, because lightning bypasses the transaction layer, and any write conflicts will be ignored silently.

review_comments: I think you should also cleanup the auto_increment attribute when create table schema to avoid auto_increment value overflow

I'm not sure if there are any users who rely on the `auto_increment` in table schema.🤔

When we really need `increment-import`, it mostly means the table already contains data and the schema has been created before. (except for parallel-import)
